content: For the past few days I have been running a "redteam" on Tau Ceti, which essentially is agents going through who get rewarded for finding mistakes or issues in Tau Ceti. Below is what they have found so far. It seems we need to consider tightening up the reuse rubric/system as we are getting some duplication.

Red-team audit of merged Tau Ceti code: results so far

Since 28 Sep an AI red-team agent (Claude, with GPT via Codex as a second opinion) has been re-auditing files that are already on main, i.e. code that passed the review pipeline. Each declaration is checked in eight categories (correctness, generality, reuse, proof, naming, API, docs, hygiene). Every finding needs a compiled Lean probe, and MAJOR findings are also cross-checked by the second model.

Scale

  • 40 files fully audited (3,041 declarations), plus follow-up sweeps for the same pattern in neighbouring files.
  • 661 findings: 0 CRITICAL, 19 MAJOR, 419 MINOR, 223 NIT.
  • 337 fixes merged, 54 in open PRs, 239 confirmed and queued, 20 waiting on a human decision.
  • 6 claims were refuted, 2 of them MAJOR (listed below).

How often a file has a MAJOR problem

  • 15 of 40 fully audited files (37.5%) had at least one confirmed MAJOR finding: 9/18 (50%) in the first session, 6/22 (27%) in the second.
  • Two more MAJORs were found by pattern sweeps into files that were not fully audited. Counting those files, the rate is 17/42 (40%).
  • No CRITICAL findings: nothing audited states something false or vacuous.

The 17 confirmed MAJOR findings, and how each was fixed

A second construction of something the library already had (12)

  1. Sl2Std.rankOneGroupScheme (Sl2/Kostant, ~870 lines over 2 files) rebuilt SlStd.groupScheme 1. Deleted the copy and moved the rank-one Weyl representative onto the type-A carrier: TauCeti#12277
  2. w1pSubmodule (Sobolev W^{1,p}) is equal to GraphStep's closed weak-derivative graph pulled back along a 3-line map. Redefined it as that comap: TauCeti#12337 (approved, in the queue)
  3. hessianOperator (Morse) was a second definition of iteratedGradientChain f 1 (Sobolev). Defined one as the other: TauCeti#12007
  4. referenceSubgroupFourMulEquivDihedralGroupFour rebuilt, with ten private helpers, an identification the library already had. Now built from the existing 4T3 identification: TauCeti#10039
  5. presentedProfiniteGroup.congr and presentedProP.congr were two hand-built copies of ContinuousMulEquiv.quotientCongr: TauCeti#12205
  6. ConnectedCoverIso was Mathlib's IsIsomorphic under a new name. Deleted: TauCeti#10161
  7. posDiagCoordinates (private) duplicated the public posDiagLowerRegion: TauCeti#10055
  8. realCliffordNegIndexEquiv (private) was Mathlib's finAddFlip: TauCeti#12176
  9. GridState.columnOfRow duplicated GridState.transpose: TauCeti#10257
  10. GridRectangle.columnSquares/rowSquares/squares duplicated coveredColumns/coveredRows/coveredSquares (equal by rfl): TauCeti#9985
  11. OrientedPDCode.crossing restated the parent structure's PDCode.crossing: TauCeti#10094
  12. FiniteQuadraticModule.adjointEquiv restated the parent's FiniteBilinearModule.adjointEquiv: TauCeti#10150

A structure field that the other axioms already imply (3)
13–15. ExactK0, AbelianK0 and TriangulatedK0.Additivap_iso field. Additivity on split exact sequences /distinguished triangles already implies it, so every construction proved it for nothing. The field is now derived: TauCeti#10242, TauCeti#10249

Other (2)
16. Wkp.instNormedSpace / instNormedAddCommGroup: these shortcut instances sit on a chain of @[reducible] defs and were never found at concrete orders, so arithmetic on W^{k,p} failed to elaborate: TauCeti#11911
17. SmoothDiscreteTopRep's docstring claimed an equivalence that only holds for topological groups, while the declaration allows any topological monoid: TauCeti#12229

Refuted MAJOR claims (our losses)

  • realCliffordForm vs QuadraticForm.realSignatureForm: the different carriers are deliberate (Fin (p+q) for the Clifford roadmap, Fin p ⊕ Fin q for Sylvester), and they are bridged by an Equivalent lemma.
  • SpStd.groupScheme 0 = SlStd.groupScheme 1: true, but it is the exceptional isomorphism C₁ = A₁ at the degenerate end of a family, not a duplicate construction.

Suggestions: catching duplication before merge
Duplication is the most common serious problem: 12 of the 17 MAJORs, and 94 findings overall (12 MAJOR, 81 MINOR, 1 NIT) are reuse failures.

  1. Search Tau Ceti, not just Mathlib. 10 of the 12 duplicated MAJORs copied Tau Ceti's own code, sometimes code merged the day before (posDiagCoordinates vs posDiagLowerRegion). The reuse rubric could require a grep of Tau Ceti for the defining term and the statement's shape, alongside the Mathlib search.
  2. Add a mechanical duplicate check to CI. For each new def, flag existing defs of the same type whose body is syntactically identical or equal by rfl. This would have caught GridRectangle.squares (rfl-equal to coveredSquares) and realCliffordNegIndexEquiv (exactly finAddFlip's body).
  3. Look for the general form before building a special case. Ask "is this the n = 1 / identity / trivial case of something already built?" The Sl2 carrier was SlStd.groupScheme 1, hessianOperator was iteratedGradientChain f 1, and w1pSubmodule is the GraphStep construction at the identity map.
  4. Check declarations on extending structures. A child-structure declaration that restates a parent's field or def is a duplicate, because dot notation already reaches the parent (OrientedPDCode.crossing, FiniteQuadraticModule.adjointEquiv).
  5. Review private declarations for reuse too. Private scaffolding that re-implements public API gets less scrutiny (posDiagCoordinates, realCliffordNegIndexEquiv).
  6. When a duplicate is found, sweep for its siblings.The profinite-presentation congr existed twice (profinite and pro-p); deduplicating one copy but not the other leaves the problem half-fixed.
    Duplication among the MINOR findings: rebuilt instead of reused (24), reprovable in a line from existing API (14), duplicate definitions (11), duplicated helpers (4).
I think most of these are an easy fix, since it seems the reuse rubric was just running at the wrong times/not looking at tau ceti itself.

Very nice!

I wonder if we should work out how to scale this up to run over everything. (Obviously first we should improve the reuse rubric.)

It would also be very interesting to run this experiment on Mathlib to get a baseline.
Oh I'd not thought about mathlib, I can definitely run it there!

Ok so mathlib has some of these issues as well, one was maybe bigger (ironically to do with modular forms, but not one of mine), but the duplication stuff is there but maybe more minor issues. I've made some draft PRs for them so people can have a look. It would be useful to get some second opinions on if these count as things we should be fixing. They sounded reasonable to me, but most are in parts of mathlib that I dont know well so there could be good reasons for them.

Critical (wrong definition)

  • ModularForm.L: L f s = Λ f s · 2/Γ_ℂ(s) gives 0 at s = 0 because of division by Γ_ℂ(0) = 0, but the true value there is −a₀ whenever the constant term a₀ ≠ 0 (e.g. L(E₄, 0) = −1), so L f is discontinuous at 0: #44547

Major (a second definition of something Mathlib already has)

  • Inclusion.IntervalDyadicReal.midpoint re-implements core's Dyadic.shiftRight (a + b) 1: #44582
  • SchwartzMap.derivCLM is built from scratch with its own seminorm estimate, but it is lineDerivOpCLM 𝕜 𝓢(ℝ, F) 1: #44583
  • Path.Homotopy.transReflReparamAux and its four helper lemmas rebuild unitInterval.qRight (t, 0): #44584
  • unitInterval.path01 is Path.id: #44589
  • CategoryTheory.Limits.piFunctor / sigmaFunctor duplicate piConst / sigmaConst in the same file (merged): #44592
  • List.Vector.zipWith duplicates List.Vector.map₂: #44593
  • Equiv.uniqueEmbeddingEquivResult duplicates Function.Embedding.oneEmbeddingEquiv: #44595
  • NumberField.mixedEmbedding.fundamentalCone.equivFinRank is a word-for-word copy of NumberField.Units.equivFinRank: #44597

Minor

  • NonUnitalStarRingHomClass adds nothing over StarHomClass (the two are equivalent given NonUnitalRingHomClass), the same reason the other bundled star-hom classes were deprecated in #16591; deprecate it: #44575
  • Set.powersetCard.isPreprimitive_alternatingGroup assumes 3 ≤ n, but its docstring (like its Perm sibling) says 1 ≤ n, and the same proof covers n = 1, 2: #44578
  • SheafOfModules.pushforwardNatTrans_app_val_app_apply is the same @[simp] lemma as pushforwardNatTrans_app_val_app in the same file: #44580
  • nhdsGE_basis_Ico restates nhdsGE_basis (and nhdsLE_basis_Ioc restates nhdsLE_basis): #44581

The are also lots of minor/nits the agents also found. I don't really know what to do with most of these, I could make more PRs and try to get them merged, but maybe we need to look at some of these and decide which we actually care about and then only PR these, since mathlib reviewer time is quite valuable.
I should say that I won't open more mathlib PRs for the time being since I don't want to clutter the queue with all of these LLM generated PRs!

Seems like a decent number of refactor pull requests to Tau Ceti generated by this is “proof is longer than 50 lines, refactor”.

Maybe we could just have a deterministic linter on whether something exceeds 50 lines. Obviously nondeterministic LLM are worse at counting number of lines in a proof.

(I guess there should be some way to opt out…?)
